notes: Evidence for the domestic burning campaign in the 2026 awareness delivery plan; small sample, so treat as a design signal rather than proof of effect.
summary: An article published in Environmental Management on 22 April 2026 evaluated a four week pilot in Swansea that sent postcode level PM2.5 alerts by text and email asking households not to burn during poor air quality episodes. Of 49 participants, 84 percent reported avoiding burning at least once after an alert and 606 hours of avoided burning were reported, with air quality literacy rising; recruitment was low, and the authors concluded that population level reductions depend on pairing such alerts with regulation, public information and help with energy costs.
title: Peer-reviewed evaluation of a Swansea pilot finds voluntary burn alerts cut some domestic wood burning
